description: Canonical registry of the state machines that were implicit in NEXUS-OS components and the PS5GreenApple app. Human narrative: docs/10-state-machines.md. Validator: tools/statecheck/statecheck.py (runs in beta-team harness). Source refs are repo paths; app-side machines cite the greapple-v2 spec and name the upstream file in 'upstream'.

conventions.status_vocabulary: PROVEN means upstream demonstrated on hardware; READY means engineering complete here; RESEARCH means no public proof; SIMULATED means dump-backend or dry-run evidence. No surface may claim a higher tier than its evidence.
conventions.fail_loud: Every machine fails loudly BEFORE touching machine state: missing artifacts, unknown inputs, and refused guards must exit with a diagnostic and a log entry.

machines.name: Boot Intent Contract

transitions.guard: re-stage (last-staged-wins: file persists across Linux-stage runs)
selector validates JSON + target whitelist + flavor rule
chain script exec'd (M with confirm flag, L with flavor, W research)
artifacts present and guards passed (see SM-08)
artifact missing | guard refused | post-hop still alive

invariants: Writers are atomic: a hub crash mid-write can never leave a half-written intent.
The reader never executes an invalid intent: validation happens before any exec, and every decision is appended to the boot log.

Three writers (greapple-v2 nexus_write_select, nexus_boot.elf, test fixtures), one reader (nexus-boot-select.sh): the schema {version:1,target,flavor?} is the contract; writers include staged_at and staged_by.
No writer ever boots; only the Linux-stage reader dispatches.
findings: F-A: the reader ignores the 'version' field today (any version dispatches). Reserved forward-compat check — do not silently extend the schema.
F-C: last-staged-wins — a stale intent from a previous session re-dispatches on the next Linux-stage run. The hub should surface staged_at age (see greapple-v2 status line).

machines.name: Hub App Lifecycle

transitions.guard: shutdown draw finishes; main loop exits cleanly

invariants: The main loop only exits through DS_SHUTDOWN — no early abort path skips resource disposal.
All input routes through the sandboxed desktop frame; no handler touches hardware state directly.
DS_SLEEP is the only state where the shell is re-enterable by a bare click; every other wait state has an explicit affordance.

machines.name: Boot Animation Phase
invariants: DONE fires exactly once (S_active flag) and hands DS_BOOT -> DS_RUN in SM-02.
boot_skip is the user escape hatch: animation can always be cut short, never restarted mid-run.

machines.name: OS Persona Router
invariants: greapple-v2 Patch 2: from v2.1 the persona switch is COSMETIC FEEDBACK ONLY (Settings -> Theme preview) and must never be mistaken for a boot action — staging is SM-01.
No transition pass: a persona change restyles the canvas in one frame; there is no intermediate state to observe.
findings: F-D history note: in v2.0.1 this router WAS the hub's fake boot; the greapple-v2 patch plan demotes it. Kept here because the demotion is itself a state-machine change agents must respect.

machines.name: Boot Camp Volume Row
machines.upstream: Blackbatman/PS5GreenApple src/app_bootcamp.c; behavior specified by greapple-v2 Patch 3

transitions.guard: bare FW userland (no shell, no block info)

invariants: STAGE AS BOOT TARGET is enabled ONLY when a declared chain can consume the volume — never a dead button.
LOCKED_BY_POLICY is permanent for internal NVMe (upstream blocks internal SSD on purpose); the row still renders.
Classification labels reuse the global status vocabulary; no row may claim more than its chain's tier.

machines.name: Permission Gate Request
invariants: Construction refuses any policy whose default is not 'deny' (ValueError) — the gate has no open mode.
Every decision (including denials and queue events) is appended to the JSONL log.
Malformed HTTP JSON is a 400 at the transport layer; it never creates a request object.
The 8-scenario selftest covers: allow-rule, queue, approve, unknown guest, traversal, bad action, operator deny, malformed input.
findings: F-B: policy declares approval_timeout_minutes=30 but nothing enforces it — WAITING_APPROVAL is unbounded until a human acts. Intentional for now; implement the timeout only with an explicit operator decision and a log event for expiry.

machines.name: Voice Intent Parse

transitions.guard: boot verb + flavor only (flavor implies linux)
bare boot verb (target stays null; hub shows OS grid)

invariants: The guard order above IS the precedence: boot > power > gate > status. Preserve it when editing the regexes.
The parser returns action JSON, never shell strings; injection-shaped input ('boot; rm -rf /') lands in INTENT_BOOT_BARE with target null and no leaked text (selftest-enforced).
Linux flavors whitelist matches chainload-linux.sh exactly (8 entries).

machines.name: Chain Arming Guards

transitions.guard: unknown option or missing required arg
artifacts present (real mode: chain M stage1; chain L kernel+initrd; chain W payload+bootmgfw)
chain M: --i-know-this-crashes-the-host AND uid=0 (chains L/W: no extra confirm by design)
chain M: sysrq-c taken | chain L: kexec -e | chain W: uefi handoff
chain M only: shell still alive after sysrq-c

invariants: No script changes machine state before ALL its guards pass: missing artifacts fail loudly first.
--dry-run is always safe and prints the exact would-run commands; the beta harness runs it in CI.
Chain M's crash hop is a controlled panic by design; STILL_ALIVE_FAIL exists to diagnose a crash kernel that was not taken.
Every dispatch decision is appended to the boot log (SM-01).

machines.name: Hub Demo Boot Modal
invariants: The demo is a SIMULATION: every banner carries the honest marker and must keep mirroring the real chain stage labels (docs/03) — demo states may not out-claim the registry.
DONE_BANNER text states what upstream proved vs what stays simulated.
findings: F-E: the macOS modal steps (7) and docs/03 chain M steps (0-8, nine rows) are not 1:1 in granularity; labels match in meaning. Keep parity in mind when either side changes.

machines.name: Feature Harness Session

transitions.guard: session picks exactly ONE passes:false feature
check passes with quoted evidence (run-tests or feature-specific)

invariants: A feature becomes VERIFIED only with passing test output shown BEFORE feature_list.json is edited.
Every VERIFIED entry carries an evidence string naming the exact check.
Progress notes are appended every session (agents/claude-progress.txt) — the notes are the team's memory.

machines.name: Workspace Init

transitions.guard: git + python3 + bash + node all present (else exit 1)
repos cloned or skipped (NEXUS_NO_NET=1; failures warn, never abort)

invariants: Missing required tools abort hard; optional tools (r2, jq, gcc) warn only.
Network fetches happen only here, only into third_party/, and are approval-gated by policy.
